evals.prompt: A colleague pasted the claims of a granted US patent into our thread (the publication number is redacted; the front page shows kind code B2). Claim 1: "A method comprising: receiving a natural-language query; generating a ranked passage set with a neural ranking model; and transmitting the ranked passage set with a per-passage confidence score." Claims 2-9 depend from it (claim 2 limits the model to a cross-encoder; claim 5 limits the index to an approximate-nearest-neighbour structure; claim 7 depends from claims 1 and 5), and claims 10 and 12 are an apparatus and a computer-readable-medium claim. What does independent claim 1 actually cover, how broad does the transitional language make it, and what do the dependent claims fall back to?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Identifies jurisdiction and status from the kind code (US ... B2 = granted); Counts independent and dependent claims and builds the dependency tree; States the transitional phrase and whether the scope is open or closed per MPEP 2111.03; Lists claim 1's elements verbatim and names the element a competitor could omit; Does not read the abstract or title as the invention.
expectations: Identifies jurisdiction and status from the kind code (US ... B2 = granted)
Counts independent and dependent claims and builds the dependency tree
States the transitional phrase and whether the scope is open or closed per MPEP 2111.03
Lists claim 1's elements verbatim and names the element a competitor could omit
Does not read the abstract or title as the invention

evals.prompt: A competitor says its new retrieval product is patent-pending. Here is the published application text — how much of our roadmap would actually read on these claims?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Works from the claim text rather than the announcement; Treats a published application as pending, not granted; Walks the elements of the broadest independent claim to test whether a product reads on it; Marks any infringement-shaped conclusion for human review rather than asserting it.
expectations: Works from the claim text rather than the announcement
Treats a published application as pending, not granted
Walks the elements of the broadest independent claim to test whether a product reads on it
Marks any infringement-shaped conclusion for human review rather than asserting it

evals.prompt: Someone pasted the claims of a pending patent application into our thread — claim 1 is a method comprising three steps and there are nine dependent claims after it. Is claim 1 broad, and are there drafting problems like means-plus-function wording or indefinite terms?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Parses numbered claims and classifies each as independent or dependent; Flags means-plus-function language under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and relative terms under MPEP 2173.05(b); Reports claim length and element count as a breadth proxy; Flags forward, dangling or improper multiple dependencies.
expectations: Parses numbered claims and classifies each as independent or dependent
Flags means-plus-function language under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and relative terms under MPEP 2173.05(b)
Reports claim length and element count as a breadth proxy
Flags forward, dangling or improper multiple dependencies

evals.prompt: Who owns the intellectual property around solid-state battery manufacturing, and is the filing rate across all those companies still accelerating?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Tallies families per assignee across the cluster and reads filing velocity (read-patent-landscape behaviour); Does not dissect the claims of a single filing.
expectations: Tallies families per assignee across the cluster and reads filing velocity (read-patent-landscape behaviour)
Does not dissect the claims of a single filing

evals.prompt: Broadcom announced it is acquiring the sensor division of Meridian Instruments for $1.4 billion in cash, expected to close in Q3, partly for its patent portfolio.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Extracts acquirer, target, consideration type, deal value and expected close (detect-ma-event behaviour); Does not parse claim text or report claim counts.
expectations: Extracts acquirer, target, consideration type, deal value and expected close (detect-ma-event behaviour)
Does not parse claim text or report claim counts
